posts.name: Jay yadav
posts.cooked:
Dear Instructor,

I am writing to formally request a manual review of my submission for oppe_1.4 in the recent system commands oppe

My submission was marked incorrect by the automated evaluator due to a syntax error (invalid reference \1), despite the fact that the code is logically correct and functions perfectly .

1. Discrepancy Between Exam Environment and Grader During the exam, I verified my script inside the provided VM terminal by making a sample question file and running my sed script on it . It produced the correct output without errors. The fact that the Automated Grader returned a syntax error indicates a critical configuration mismatch: the student environment runs a standard version of sed, while the grader appears to be running a restrictive or outdated version.

2. Technical Correctness of the Solution My script utilizes the \L and \U escape sequences for case conversion.

  • Standard Practice: These are standard features of GNU sed, which is the default version on virtually all modern Linux distributions (Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, RHEL).

  • Validity: Since this course focuses on Linux, using standard GNU tools is appropriate and correct practice. The error suggests the grader is enforcing strict POSIX compliance without supporting common modern extensions.

Conclusion It is unfair to be penalized for writing code that is a) correct by modern industry standards and b) functional within the environment provided to students for testing.

I respectfully request that my solution be evaluated based on its logic and functionality within the standard Linux environment provided during the exam.

My Code:

s/^low:\(.*\)/\L\1/

s/^up:\(.*\)/\U\1/

Thank you for your time in reviewing this matter.

Sincerely, jay yadav , [23f3002231]

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
Dear student, I have gone through your submission.

Did you read the question carefully?

Screenshot 2025-12-10 at 21.10.431672×784 162 KB

The question mentions how your script is run, did you test it this way? It specifies we will default to ERE (Extended Regular Expression Engine) for Regex. Why does your code use BRE then?

The problem is not any mismatch in evaluator or POSIX sed being used (how did you even come up with such conclusions? did you even check or are you simply speculating? We do not have any other sed other than GNU sed installed in the VM, and we do not run it in POSIX compliance mode, a simple view of the evaluation_file.sh would have shown you that), rather your code does not have any backreference at all. You are escaping your groups ( \( and \) ) which is not required in ERE. Please be familiar with the basics of ERE for OPPE. You are trying to match literal parentheses, instead of creating groups.

Your solution would have been correct if you had not escaped the (). There is no issues with the evaluator, it cannot guess what regex engine you are using, so it is explicitly mentioned to use ERE in the question.

Please introspect your own code before coming up with these speculations. 570 students have got 100 marks in this question by correctly solving the question, showing no issues in evaluation.

I would recommend inculcating debugging skill, as it is highly useful in timed programming exams with immediate evaluation for fixing issues with your code:

23f3002231:

invalid reference \1

This clearly lets you know that the sed is not non-standard and does know what a back-reference is. Further, it states clearly that even though you use \1 in your code, there are no groups defined in the regex to refer to as group 1. Which then leads you to debug your escaping mistake.

Hope this clarifies your misunderstanding.

Regards,
Sayan
Course Team
